title: Open Source Edge0 Model Brings 145 Billion Parameter AI to a Single Laptop, and Businesses Should Pay Attention
summary: Edge0 open-source model brings 145-billion-parameter AI to a single laptop
detailed: AI developer Edge0 released Edge0-145B and Edge0-120B, sparse open-source models designed to run entirely on personal computers without cloud connectivity.
Edge0-145B features 10 billion active parameters per step, a peak memory footprint of 29 gigabytes, and decoding speeds exceeding 80 tokens per second on consumer hardware.
Concurrently, Google released Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a fast lower-cost model running 2.5 times faster than its predecessor and integrated into developer workflows via the Antigravity platform.
Google's Antigravity pairs a larger Carbon model for planning with Hydrogen for execution, establishing a template for balancing cost and reasoning capability.
These developments matter because they signal an industry shift toward localized on-device AI and tiered model architectures that optimize operational costs for businesses.
sentences: On November 12, AI developer Edge0 released two large language models, Edge0-145B and Edge0-120B, along with the inference software and deployment tools needed to run them.
The company says Edge0-145B is the first open-source model of its size designed to run entirely on a personal computer, with no cloud connection required.
The technical claims are specific.
The model uses a sparse expert design, so only about 10 billion of its 145 billion parameters are active at any given step.
Edge0 reports a peak memory footprint of 29 gigabytes, decoding speeds above 80 tokens per second, typical power draw near 120 watts, and context windows from 128,000 to 256,000 tokens.
Compatible hardware includes MacBook Pro laptops with Apple M-series chips and Windows machines with high-end consumer graphics cards.
Edge0 also says the model scores competitively with frontier cloud models on coding, reasoning, and agent benchmarks.
An important caution: those benchmark results come from Edge0’s own internal testing.
Independent evaluations have not yet confirmed them.

German outlet KIberblick also noted that while Edge0 calls the release open source, the model ships under a custom license called the Edge0 Community Model License 1.0, so businesses should read the terms before building anything on it.
The outlet’s advice for teams is to experiment internally but wait for independent tests before making a decision.
Small and mid-sized businesses do not need to rush.
A sensible first step is to assign one technical person to test the model on a non-sensitive task and compare the output quality against the cloud tools you already use.
Review the license for any restrictions on commercial use.
Check whether your current computers meet the memory and graphics requirements, since a 29 gigabyte footprint rules out many standard office machines.
The larger takeaway is the direction of travel.

Capable AI is moving from rented cloud services toward software businesses can own and run themselves, and companies that start learning how to deploy it locally will be better positioned as that shift continues.

The Gap Comes Down to Measurement
Google’s new fast model replaces its Flash tier across Search, the Gemini app and developer tools, and it arrives with a built-in way to pay only for the thinking you need.
Google released Gemini 4 Hydrogen on November 12, 2026.
It replaces Gemini 3.8 Flash as the company’s fast, lower-cost model and is built for everyday coding and multi-step agent work such as research, data analysis and testing.
Google says it runs about 2.5 times faster than Gemini 3.8 Flash at a high reasoning setting.
Hydrogen is live in Google Search worldwide, the Gemini app, Google AI Studio, the Gemini API and Google’s Antigravity development platform.
The most useful part of this launch is not the speed.
It is the way Google is pairing models.
In Antigravity, a new Orchestrator tool uses the larger Gemini 4 Carbon model to plan the work and Hydrogen to carry out edits and tests.
That is a practical template for any company building AI workflows: use the expensive model for the hard thinking, and the cheap, fast model for the repetitive steps.
For small and mid-sized businesses, that approach can bring down the cost of running AI receptionists, support agents and back office automations.
Not every customer call or form needs the most powerful model available, and the four reasoning levels give teams a dial to tune cost against quality.
The AI market is shifting from one model for everything toward teams of models matched to the job.
Businesses that learn to mix fast and powerful models will get better results for less money than those that default to the biggest model every time.
Sources: Google announcement of Gemini 4 Hydrogen, Google Antigravity blog, and coverage from Ars Technica and other outlets, November 12 and 13, 2026.

As Microsoft struggles to restore Outlook, Teams, and Microsoft 365 following a major worldwide outage, individuals and businesses can protect their communications, restore productivity, and keep everyday life moving with free alternatives such as Gmail, Google Meet, Zoom, and other reliable digital services.
The global Microsoft outage of November 12 and 13, 2026, has delivered an important reminder about the technology millions of people depend on every day.

From business correspondence and virtual meetings to school assignments, professional appointments, and everyday personal communication, modern life relies on digital services that people expect to be available whenever they need them.
When those systems become inaccessible, the consequences can extend well beyond an inconvenient morning at the office.
Work can be interrupted, important messages delayed, appointments missed, and families left struggling to communicate.
The disruption affecting Microsoft’s widely used cloud services has reached businesses, government agencies, educational institutions, and individual users across multiple countries.

Microsoft Outlook, Exchange Online, Teams, and several other Microsoft 365 services have experienced problems, leaving users unable to access email, retrieve information, schedule meetings, or complete certain digital tasks.
The scale of the incident has demonstrated how deeply Microsoft technology is integrated into everyday professional and personal activities.
As of the morning of Friday, November 13, 2026, the outage had not been confirmed as fully resolved.

Microsoft was reporting meaningful progress in restoring affected infrastructure, including improving server stability, service availability, and email delivery across North America, Europe, and the Asia-Pacific region.
However, intermittent access problems and delayed messages remained possible as engineers continued repairs.
The situation was improving, but a complete return to normal service could not yet be guaranteed.
For anyone wondering whether Microsoft Outlook is working again, the answer depends partly on the particular service, account, and region involved.
Some users have regained access while others may continue to encounter errors or delays.

Microsoft’s public service-status website, https://status.cloud.microsoft, provides general information, while organizations using Microsoft 365 should consult the Service Health section of their administrative dashboard for details about their own services.
A general operational notice for consumer products does not necessarily mean that every business Microsoft 365 service has recovered.
The immediate concern for millions of people is remarkably practical.

How can someone continue receiving important messages, attending appointments, participating in video conferences, communicating with colleagues, and maintaining everyday responsibilities when a major technology provider becomes unavailable?
Fortunately, there are several accessible solutions, many of them free, that can help users remain connected while Microsoft completes its recovery.
A significant lesson from the outage is that digital convenience should be accompanied by a degree of independence.

Keeping an alternative email address, understanding how to join meetings through another platform, and maintaining secure copies of important documents can make the difference between a temporary inconvenience and a prolonged interruption.
